newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian cement company in partial flotation.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian cement company in partial flotation.

text.p: The founders of a new cement company in southern Egypt on Wednesday offered 10.5 million shares or 30 percent of the firm for sale to the public at a price of 10 pounds per share.

Founders of South Valley Cement Company (SVCC) said the public offer would be open to Egyptians and foreigners for two months starting from July 20 and would close after a minimum of 10 days if the offer is oversubscribed.
Individual investors must apply for at least 50 shares, while institutions have a 1,000-share minimum.
Investors can pay for the shares they want by installments, the announcement said. There is an issuance fee of 0.10 pounds per share.
SVCC was established by the Egyptian Saudi Group for South Valley Projects and has an issued capital of 350 million pounds ($100 million) with total investments of 850 million.
The founders include Banque Misr, two British companies, a Saudi company and several individual Saudi businessmen as well as other individual shareholders.
Banque Misr is the agent for the sale.
SVCC founders said in March the company would have a production capacity of 1.4 million tonnes a year in the first stage.
They said the new plant would be set up in the Western Desert oasis of Kharga, some 550 km (340 miles) southwest of Cairo.

The cement plant would be well placed to supply construction sites associated with President Hosni Mubarak's scheme to irrigate at least 500,000 acres of land in the Western desert with water pumped in from the lake behind the Aswan High Dam.
Two other cement companies have recently said they will build plants, one of them in south Egypt.
The cement sector is highly profitable in Egypt and cement firms are among the blue chips on the stock market.
